short: Patching shows the decoder depends on donor activations, not that transfer runs through a compact subspace: kept regions score below the unpatched decoder, with no null and no held-out split.
position: The paper changes one component: it explains an sEEG Conv1D-BiGRU decoder (Sec. 4.2) by patching activations between vocalized, mimed and imagined speech (M06). Intervening on internal activations is rare (2 of 38 studies, pattern match, Appendix), but one participant and one architecture give no repetition, so by the verdict rules it is standard, not ahead. The central claim, vocalized-to-imagined transfer through a compact subspace, holds only against random blocks: the kept convolutional subspace beats a matched random block (PCC 0.666 against 0.564) but not the unpatched imagined decoder (0.725; Tables 1 and 3). Full patching gives the same PCC 0.954 and MCD 1.63 for imagined and mimed recipients, above the donor's 0.752 (Table 3), so it reflects the donor, not transfer (inference). The field's own transfer test, an overt-trained decoder applied to covert input (M04), is not reported, and no null model backs any effect (M12).
